subject: Production surge: recommended hosting path and immediate next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Gupta <rajiv.gupta@paynorth.com>
Cc: Elena Moreno <elena@paynorth.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Prod surge recap + immediate options (hosted / dedicated / private)

Rajiv — thanks for the quick sync this morning. Quick written recap and clear next steps so we don’t lose momentum.

Summary of the issue
- You observed a sustained token-rate surge starting 2026-06-19 22:40 UTC causing repeated 429s and increased p95 tail latency on the hosted endpoint.
- Current risk: continued production throttling and potential customer-impacting errors during peak batch windows.

Options we discussed (high-level)
1) Hosted API immediate mitigations (hours) — temporary: request shaping, model throttling, enable prefix caching, short-term burst credit. Low friction but not isolation.
2) Redwood Dedicated (days) — reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, isolated tenancy. Recommended if you need predictable SLAs and sustained throughput.
3) Private VPC / On-prem (weeks) — full isolation and compliance controls; longer lead time.

Recommended path (per today’s call): short-term hosted mitigations to buy ~48–72 hours, then fast-track a Dedicated trial for the next 30 days (we can provision burst capacity and target lead time of 3–7 business days if we prioritize).

Action items
- Camila (me): open urgent provisioning request and pull in Aditya + Monica to scope Dedicated fast-track and SOC2/contract asks. Attach: rapid-migration-map.xlsx, SLA request PDF.
- PayNorth (Rajiv/Elena): share estimated sustained qps and preferred peak windows (TZ, dates), and confirm willingness to sign short-term commitment for Dedicated trial.

Please reply with the qps numbers and any procurement constraints. I’ll follow up with an internal pre-req checklist and timeline.

—
Camila Reyes
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192
Redwood Inference

Attachments: rapid-migration-map.xlsx (plan), paynorth-sla-request.pdf

From: Rajiv Gupta <rajiv.gupta@paynorth.com>

Cc: PayNorth SRE Team <ops@paynorth.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Prod surge recap + immediate options (hosted / dedicated / private)

Thanks Camila — appreciate the clear breakdown. A few clarifications from our side:

- Current impact: 5% of transactions are hitting 429s during the 17:00–19:00 ET window (approx 3–4 spikes over the last 24 hours). Tail p95 latency went from ~220ms to ~1.6s on the hosted endpoint.
- Our security/compliance bar: if we move to Dedicated we need customer data logically isolated and an SLA on 99.9% uptime for inference endpoints during business hours.
- Procurement note: we can fast-track a 30-day trial if Redwood can guarantee isolation and provide SOC2 evidence and a PO-friendly MSA with limited redlines.

QPS: sustained 120 qps during peak + short bursts to 400 qps for 5–10 minutes. Average sequence length ~280 tokens.

We’re inclined to go to Dedicated if you can provision quickly and commit to an interim SLA. If Dedicated lead time is >7 business days we may need Private VPC evaluation, but that will introduce procurement and infra timelines.

—
Rajiv Gupta
Head of SRE, PayNorth
rajiv.gupta@paynorth.com

Rajiv — thanks, that qps/sequence info is super helpful. Quick update and concrete asks: 

Short-term (within 6 hours) — mitigation I’ll enact now:
- Enable prefix-level KV caching for your top-10 prompt templates (Aditya to confirm safe TTL).
- Apply conservative rate-limiter rules on the hosted route for anonymous traffic to reduce noise.
- Temporarily fall back to a smaller model variant for non-critical flows.

Mid-term (fast-track Dedicated) — proposed timeline and prerequisites:
- Target provisioning: 3–7 business days if we pull dedicated capacity from our fast-track pool. This requires: 30-day purchase commitment or trial PO, signed short addendum covering SLAs, SOC2 evidence.
- Aditya: can you confirm cluster sizing for 120 sustained qps, peaks to 400 qps, seq len 280? Also flag any quantization/model picks to reduce cost.

Attached: paynorth-sla-request.pdf (formal request) and rapid-migration-map.xlsx (high-level MAP). I’ll follow up with a short MSA redline we can accept for a short-term trial.

Next steps: Rajiv to confirm PO intent and signoff path. We’ll queue provisioning once PO received.

Quick internal notes from SRE/solutions on sizing and feasibility: 

- For 120 sustained qps and 400 qps bursts (seq=280 tokens), recommended config: 4x A100-equivalent slots with continuous batching and opportunistic KV caching. This supports p95 < 350ms under dedicated runtime with the model variant we discussed.
- Fast-track pool availability: we have limited burst headroom this week; we can allocate a 30-day trial cluster but need PO + signed short addendum by EOD Monday to lock capacity.
- Compliance: SOC2 report is available; we can provide redacted evidence and a security questionnaire response within 24 hours. Private VPC/on-prem would add ~3–6 weeks for infra set-up and procurement.

Short mitigation notes for Camila: enabling prefix caching + switching to q4_0 quantized variant for non-critical paths should buy 24–48 hours of headroom. I’ll ping infra to pre-stage images if we get PO.

—
